context: Start at ground level, 0. Each move still climbs 1 or 2 stairs, and the goal is stair 3. The new constraint is that two consecutive moves cannot both climb 1 stair.
description: The stairs are numbered 0 through 6. The tread of the target stair, 3, is green. A gray dotted line traces 0→1→2→3. The label above it reads, “Two consecutive moves cannot both climb 1 stair, so discard 0→1→2→3.” A solid blue line highlights 0→2→3, and a solid orange line highlights 0→1→3. The note below reads, “There are two ways to reach stair 3: 0→2→3 and 0→1→3.”

frames.explanation: The route 0→1→2→3 takes three one-stair moves in succession. The first two already violate the rule, so the route is grayed out. The blue route, 0→2→3, climbs 2 stairs then 1. The orange route, 0→1→3, climbs 1 then 2. Both are valid because neither has consecutive one-stair moves.
frames.title: Ways to reach stair 3 without climbing one stair twice in a row

summary: The rule against consecutive one-stair moves rules out 0→1→2→3, leaving just two ways to reach stair 3.
title: Ways to reach stair 3 without climbing one stair twice in a row
